label: l/3/z/k/q input early in the original phase after a prefix of g/r/t/s/y/x-type tokens
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (90% of mass) plus the <DEL> step (10%). It is essentially silent in the copy phase and at t=0-1, and peaks at t=3-4. Two things drive it: the current input token (l is strongest at 9x lift, then 3, z, k, q) and the earlier prefix. It is strongest when nearly all earlier inputs come from a set of tokens (g, r, t, s, y, x, i, u, j, n, 1, p). first_tok and prev2_tok both show 3x lift for g/r/t/s/y/x. The top activations are all l or 3 at t=3-4 after prefixes like r g t 1 or g s 1. It rarely fires on repeated tokens (in_first=0 carries 4% of mass). The same l/z/3 input after other prefixes usually does not fire. The predicate gets only about 0.4 F1, which suggests the unit reads a graded hidden-state direction rather than a crisp rule. Precision is limited because the token-set prefix condition is only an approximation, and recall misses the <DEL>-step firings and other input tokens.
